title: Klook Strengthens Flash Sale Protection Against Malicious Bots While Supporting Legitimate AI
content:
Klook is a leading global platform for experiences where customers book tours and experiences, attraction tickets, events, hotels, transport, and travel essentials such as WiFi and SIM cards.

Klook’s Payments & Fraud team is responsible for fraud prevention, bot mitigation, and payment risk management, with a focus on protecting the platform while maintaining a seamless experience for legitimate customers.

As automated threats become increasingly sophisticated, traditional rule-based approaches alone are no longer sufficient. Klook combines its internal fraud prevention strategies and security infrastructure with DataDome as an additional layer of AI-powered bot detection and mitigation, particularly for high-demand ticket sales.

During major events, DataDome’s SOC and Galileo Threat Research teams work alongside Klook to monitor suspicious traffic, investigate emerging attack patterns, and support ongoing improvements to protection strategies.

“Bot attacks evolve constantly, and static rules alone are not enough. DataDome gives us an additional layer of detection and mitigation that complements our internal fraud prevention.”
Klook Payments & Fraud Team

The challenge: Attacks that keep changing shape

As Klook’s business continues to grow, automated threats are constantly evolving. During high-demand ticket sales, identifying and mitigating malicious bot activity while maintaining a seamless experience for genuine customers remains a key challenge.

Flash sales create additional pressure on the platform, as large volumes of automated traffic can affect platform stability and the experience of customers trying to access and purchase tickets.

Another emerging challenge is traffic generated by AI-powered browser tools and agents. As these technologies evolve, distinguishing legitimate automation from malicious bot activity becomes increasingly important.

The Klook Payments & Fraud team explains: “The key challenge is to distinguish legitimate automation from malicious activity without unnecessarily restricting genuine users or legitimate AI use cases.”

The solution: An additional layer of protection, working together

DataDome Bot Protect is integrated into Klook’s web traffic protection architecture, providing an additional layer of detection and mitigation for selected web and API traffic.

Its AI-powered detection models help identify suspicious automated behaviour, particularly in high-demand ticketing scenarios.

“DataDome's AI-powered detection models help us identify and mitigate automated traffic, particularly during high-demand ticket sales.”
Klook Payments & Fraud team

Klook’s internal teams continue to oversee the broader risk management strategy, combining DataDome’s detection capabilities with internal fraud prevention policies, platform security controls, and business-specific risk measures.

For major ticket sales, Klook and DataDome collaborate ahead of key events. DataDome’s SOC and Threat Research teams provide additional support by investigating suspicious traffic, analysing attack patterns, and helping refine mitigation strategies.

This collaborative approach allows Klook to strengthen protection while balancing platform security, operational stability, and customer experience.

The results: Continuous improvement through collaboration

The collaboration with DataDome has enhanced Klook’s visibility into automated traffic and added another layer of protection for high-demand events.

Following major sales, both teams review attack patterns, suspicious traffic, and potential false positives. Insights from these reviews help identify protection gaps and inform improvements for future events.

The Klook Payments & Fraud team says: “We look for gaps and improve our protection for future events.”

Klook has recently renewed its partnership with DataDome, reflecting its continued commitment to strengthening bot protection as automated threats evolve.

“The renewal reflects our continued need for bot protection as threats evolve.”
Klook Payments & Fraud team

Looking ahead: Preparing for the era of AI-powered travel

As AI agents become more integrated into travel discovery and booking, the way customers interact with travel platforms is expected to evolve.

The Klook Security team believes: “Travelers will increasingly discover options and complete bookings through conversations with AI agents, with fewer manual steps. The browser experience may become much simpler, with only the interactions needed to complete a task. Klook’s approach is to allow legitimate automation where appropriate while applying controls based on risk.”

They add: “Avoid blocking all automation by default. A risk-based approach balances platform protection with customer experience.”
